第 2 章 Answer These 10 Questions to Understand Whether You're a Good Manager回答这 10 个问题，看看你是不是个好经理

Cate Huston / 凯特·休斯顿

— 第 17 页 —

Something I struggled with as a new manager was finding a sense of accomplishment. It's difficult to find the right success metrics upon which to judge our work because our output is to make the team better. Without success metrics beyond the team's improvement, though, it can be easy to feel like you're just riding a wave of good people doing good work without contributing anything yourself.

刚做管理时，我一直苦于找不到成就感。很难找到合适的成功标准来衡量我们的工作，因为我们的产出就是让团队变得更好。但如果除了「团队进步」之外没有其他成功指标，你很容易觉得自己只是在搭一群优秀的人做优秀工作的顺风车，自己什么都没贡献。

Some managers deal with this feeling by seeing their success metric as being available to their teams 24/7 (unsustainable) or by counting lines of code (which would be like editors focusing on the number of words they wrote themselves—absurd). Some embrace the performance of management without understanding the underlying motivations. They "perform good manager" in one-on-one meetings, standup meetings, and feedback cycles, but it doesn't really make them feel accomplished, and it's difficult to put a finger on why.

有些管理者应对这种感觉的方式是把「24 小时随叫随到」当成自己的成功指标（不可持续），或者数自己写了多少行代码（这就像编辑盯着自己写了多少字一样荒谬）。有些人则在不理解底层动机的情况下「表演管理」。他们在一对一、站会和反馈周期里「扮演好经理」，但这并不能让他们真正有成就感，而且很难说清楚为什么。

To that end, I've compiled a list of signs that I look for in managers on my teams that suggest they're doing a good job.

为此，我整理了一份清单——我在团队管理者身上观察到的、表明他们做得不错的信号。

Can You Take a Week Off?你能休一周假吗？

There's nothing like a week off (or more!) to show which of your activities has the most impact. When you come back, pay attention to what you find. What's surprising to you? What comes up in your one-on-one meetings? What did people miss? What did they not need you for?

没有什么比休一周（或更久）假更能看出你的哪些活动真正有影响力了。回来之后，注意你发现了什么。什么让你惊讶？一对一会议里大家聊了什么？大家怀念什么？哪些事其实不需要你？

— 第 18 页 —

Can Problems Be Handled Without You?没有你，问题能被解决吗？

This is huge—you'll never get away from using constant availability as your metric if every emergency must come to you. Ensuring that everyone on the team feels a sense of responsibility and ownership, and having a clear Directly Responsible Individual (DRI) is key.

这一点至关重要——如果每个紧急事件都必须找你，你就永远无法摆脱「随叫随到」这个衡量标准。关键是让团队每个人都有责任感和主人翁意识，并且有明确的直接负责人（DRI）。

Does Your Team Deliver Consistently?你的团队能稳定交付吗？

Delivery is a trailing indicator for a healthy team, but it is an indicator. Healthy teams ship, consistently, and keep shipping over time. We all have projects that become unexpectedly complex, and every individual one might have a reasonable explanation, but if you look at the overall picture, is the team delivering more often than not?

交付是健康团队的滞后指标，但它确实是指标。健康的团队会持续发布、长期保持。我们都有项目突然变得异常复杂的时候，每个单独看都有合理的解释，但纵观全局——团队是不是大多数时候都在交付？

Do People Tell You What They Think?人们会告诉你他们的真实想法吗？

One thing that we all must get used to in leadership is people being less candid with us. We need to make ourselves available explicitly to people who don't want to presume to seek us out (these are important people to listen to; otherwise, you just hear the loudest voices).

做领导必须习惯的一件事就是：人们对你会不那么直率。我们需要主动给那些不好意思找我们的人创造沟通渠道（这些人是必须倾听的；否则你只能听到最大声的那些人）。

It's also important to note how people give you critical feedback. Do they wait until it's something they are really frustrated by? Or is it an ongoing conversation? Will people tell you what they are worried or insecure about? Will they share what they notice is going on around you?

还要注意人们怎么给你批评性反馈。他们是忍到实在受不了才说？还是日常就在持续沟通？人们会告诉你他们在担心什么、对什么没信心吗？他们会跟你分享他们注意到你周围发生的事吗？

Do People on the Team Treat Each Other Well?团队成员之间相处融洽吗？

Effective teams are inclusive teams. As a leader, it's on you to cultivate a respectful environment on your team, and to make it clear that you will not tolerate discriminatory words or behavior. This is the minimum. Beyond that, you can set some values around reward and advancement that make it clear that success on your team is something that happens interdependently, not as a competition.

高效的团队是包容的团队。作为领导，你有责任在团队中营造尊重的环境，明确表示你不容忍歧视性言论或行为。这是底线。除此之外，你还可以在奖励和晋升方面设定一些价值观，明确传达：团队的成功是相互依存的，不是零和竞争。

Is the Team Self-Improving?团队会自我改进吗？

Self-improving teams critique and iterate and change things as a part of their process. They're not afraid to discuss what worked and what didn't, make suggestions, and try changes knowing that some of the changes they make will fail.

自我改进的团队会把批评、迭代和改变当作流程的一部分。他们不怕讨论什么有效、什么无效，不怕提建议，也不怕尝试改变——即使知道有些改变会失败。

— 第 19 页 —

These teams get better over time with less and less intervention from you. It can be difficult to get teams reflecting on what went right and wrong with a project because this process is scary (and the first few times might be quite rough). But getting to a place where these "postmortems" are a matter of course is the outcome of a self-improving team.

这样的团队会越来越好，而你需要介入的越来越少。让团队复盘项目的对错可能很难，因为这个过程令人恐惧（而且前几次可能相当粗糙）。但当「事后复盘」成为理所当然的事时，就是一个自我改进团队的成熟标志。

Can You Give People Who Report to You Meaningful, In-Depth Feedback?你能给下属有意义、有深度的反馈吗？

The way I think about feedback is this: feedback is someone's work reflected back to them, in a way that helps them take pride in their accomplishments and makes actionable the places where they can improve. This means having enough insight into their work, accomplishments, and struggles to be able to do that. A lot of that feedback happens as we go, but at most, every six months I make a point to get some (qualitative or quantitative) feedback from team members that I can use to put together a bigger picture of how someone is doing.

我对反馈的理解是这样的：反馈是把一个人的工作反射回给他，既帮他为自己的成就感到自豪，也让他能具体行动起来去改进。这意味着你需要对他们的工作、成就和困境有足够深入的了解。很多反馈是日常发生的，但我最多每半年就会特意从团队成员那里收集一些（定性或定量的）反馈，用来拼凑出一个人整体表现的全貌。

What Kinds of Things Can You Delegate?你能授权哪些事？

Do you feel like you can hand off pieces of work or problems to people on your team? Are those projects growing bigger over time? Maybe you started by giving people tasks, but over time, you want to be able to give them broader problems to own. This allows you to take on more.

你觉得自己能把工作或问题交给团队成员吗？那些项目随着时间推移是不是越来越大？也许一开始你只是给人派任务，但渐渐地，你希望能把更大的问题交给他们负责。这样你自己才能承担更多。

If you manage managers and you don't have people to whom you can hand stuff off, you will drown. It's just not possible to operate effectively at that scale without the shock absorption of people being able to take things off your plate and handle them. If you don't have it, you will need to build it, because it will only get worse over time.

如果你管的是管理者，却没有人可以把事情交出去，你会被淹死。在那个规模下，没有别人帮你分担和缓冲，根本不可能有效运作。如果你还没有这个梯队，就必须去建，因为情况只会越来越糟。

Who Is Taking on Bigger Roles?谁在承担更大的角色？

As the team grows, there's more opportunity—and more need—for people to step up. Delegation flows down: pushing things onto the managers forces them to push things onto people on their teams, and this is how we grow new leaders.

随着团队扩大，人们有更多机会——也更需要——站出来承担。授权是往下流的：把事情压给管理者，就迫使他们把事情压给团队成员，新的领导者就是这样成长起来的。

As much as we might adore everyone on our team and want to keep them together, having a strong team means that sometimes people's best path for success lies outside of it. It's our job as managers to help them toward it. It's a sign of success when people from our teams go to other teams and take on more responsibility there.

尽管我们可能很喜欢团队里的每个人、想把大家留在身边，但一个强大的团队意味着有时候人们最好的成功之路在团队之外。管理者的职责就是帮他们走向那条路。当你团队的人去了别的团队、承担了更大的责任时，这恰恰是你成功的标志。

— 第 20 页 —

Can You Take on Work Outside of Your Immediate Scope?你能承担本职范围之外的工作吗？

Having our own teams in order, and strong support within them, makes it possible for us to provide more support to those above and around us. What could you take on that would most help your boss? Your peers? Can the scope of your work get bigger over time?

把自己的团队理顺、内部有强支撑，我们才有可能为上级和周围的人提供更多支持。你能承担什么最能帮到你的老板？你的平级同事？你的工作范围能随着时间扩大吗？

Do Your Peers Value Your Perspective and Come to You for Advice?你的平级同事重视你的观点并来找你请教吗？

Every organization has its own unique set of quirks, and the people who best understand the stress under which we operate are our peers. In a functional and collaborative environment, who respects whom in a peer group says a lot. Pay attention to the topics people seem to value your opinion on. It shows what they notice—which are often the things we most take for granted.

每个组织都有自己独特的怪癖，最理解我们所承受压力的人就是平级同事。在一个运转良好、协作顺畅的环境里，平级之间谁尊重谁很能说明问题。注意看人们在哪些话题上重视你的意见。这说明他们注意到了什么——而那些往往是我们最理所当然的事。
